disease_label_per_paper: Serum sickness-like reaction associated with acute hepatitis B in a previously vaccinated adult male
presentation_summary: 36-year-old man with active intravenous heroin use, shared needles, chronic untreated hepatitis C, documented prior HAV/HBV vaccination, and household exposure to a male friend with chronic hepatitis B presented with two weeks of swelling, stiffness, and tenderness of knees, ankles, MCP, and PIP joints.

He had three days of painful pruritic rash on the feet spreading to the lower abdomen, genital area, and upper limbs; examination showed non-blanching erythematous macular rash, knee effusions/tenderness, ankle tenderness/restricted motion, cervical spine tenderness, and symmetric MCP/PIP tenderness.
Initial vital signs were afebrile 36.7 C, BP 142/87 mmHg, HR 104/min, RR 18/min; initial exam was negative for jaundice, abdominal distension, and ascites.
Initial labs showed AST 375 U/L, ALT 502 U/L, ESR 40 mm/hr, CRP 13 mg/L, INR 1.09, BUN 16 mg/dL, creatinine 0.5 mg/dL.
Two days into admission he developed abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, and diffuse abdominal tenderness without hepatosplenomegaly.

Workup showed low C4 with normal C3, negative cryoglobulins, ANCA, urinalysis, blood cultures, and HAV IgM; hepatitis B panel was positive for HBsAg, HBeAg, and IgM anti-HBc, with HBV DNA 214 million IU/mL.

The paper diagnosed serum sickness-like reaction associated with acute hepatitis B infection; he left hospital against medical advice after symptomatic treatment, and follow-up showed symptom resolution, HBsAg negativity, anti-HBe positivity, and HBV DNA <10 IU/mL.
